title: Segunda Guerra Mundial: a batalha da propaganda em Portugal
content:
De um lado, um Winston Churchill caricatural, de semblante derrotado, senta-se sobre a campa do Império Britânico enquanto é banhado por um sol marcado por uma suástica. Do outro, um boneco do icónico governente inglês encara-nos com um olhar confiante com esse mesmo símbolo nazi tatuado nos genitais, metáfora satírica do recuo alemão face ao avanço inglês. Estes são dois exemplos contrastantes com o mesmo fim — produzir propaganda durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial — mas têm algo muito específico que os reveste de especial interesse: foram concebidos para influenciar o povo português.
Portugal foi dos poucos estados a manter a neutralidade quando quase todo o mundo se precipitou para o maior conflito da história da humanidade, mas isso não quer dizer que o país não tenha sido um campo de batalha da semântica e da retórica pela conquista da opinião pública. Com abertura ao público esta terça-feira, 22 de setembro, no Parque Empresarial do Barreiro, a exposição A Outra Guerra, Propaganda em Português na Segunda Guerra Mundial, organizada pelo Arquivo Ephemera, espelha esse esforço em quase 600 peças originais.
Na azáfama dos últimos preparativos, José Pacheco Pereira explica numa visita guiada ao Observador que, no arquivo que gere, um dos maiores de natureza privada do país, reside uma “grande coleção de material da Segunda Guerra Mundial”. Desse manancial de fontes documentais foi escolhida “uma pequeníssima parte” para esta exposição com “um aspeto em comum: salvo uma ou outra exceção, está em português e foi feito para Portugal”.
“A primeira coisa que me surpreendeu foi a importância que Portugal tinha na propaganda, quer dos Aliados quer das potências do Eixo”, afirma o fundador da Associação Cultural Ephemera. Esse foco na “conquista das almas” portuguesas — como o também historiador descreve no texto introdutório desta mostra — está bem patente nos materiais que é possível ver espalhados por várias mesas.
Em alguns núcleos, o foco de postais, panfletos, livros e cartazes está em destacar o desenvolvimento económico e social dos respetivos lados; noutros, o intuito é de valorizar as mais recentes conquistas, especialmente por meio de revistas militares de grafismo triunfal. Uma das mesas é dominada por loas panegíricas aos “Senhores da Guerra”: Roosevelt, Churchill, Hitler — todos menos Estaline, por razões que mais à frente ficarão bem claras. Noutra podemos atentar em como alguns dos principais discursos destes líderes foram transcritos, traduzidos e comercializados em Portugal.
“Quando começamos a ver a importância desta coleção, começámos a perceber padrões e achámos que a exposição podia revelar esses padrões e, portanto, acrescentar alguma coisa ao conhecimento histórico desta época”, afirma Pacheco Pereira. Dessa forma, fica claro que o foco inglês está em destacar “a ideia de estabilidade política associada à família real, que aparece, aliás, fardada e associada às iniciativas de guerra”. Já os americanos distinguem-se ao fazer sobretudo “o elogio da sua própria democracia” contra o totalitarismo. “São os defensores da liberdade em todo o mundo e, portanto, têm uma propaganda politicamente diferente dos ingleses”, conta.
Já o lado alemão, continua Pacheco Pereira, “abrange aspectos muito mais variados do que a propaganda dos Aliados”. “Não é uma mera propaganda de guerra, há muita importância dada aos feitos civis, ao papel dos operários e à capacidade que o regime tinha para lhes dar uma boa vida”, fazendo-o sobretudo em contraponto ao que denunciavam como a “miséria do bolchevismo” existente na União Soviética. Essa defesa da superioridade germânica, aponta, também se vê nos materiais onde se destaca a robustez da economia alemã perante as tentativas de bloqueio comercial britânico. No lado inglês, aponta-se sobretudo para as perdas humanas e materiais dos nazis.
No decurso da visita, o responsável pela Ephemera explica que a grande maioria destes materiais foi produzida ou encomendada pelas embaixadas e delegações das potências beligerantes, muitas vezes aproveitando as mais recentes novidades do conflito para reforçar o seu esforço propagandístico. Uma das mesas demonstra este aspeto com exemplos do final da guerra: se os nazis começaram a produzir materiais a denunciar o massacre de Katyn — no qual os soviéticos executaram milhares de oficiais polacos em 1940 —, os Aliados aprontaram-se a demonstrar os horrores do Holocausto ao divulgar as valas comuns dos campos de concentração que foram libertando e que ainda não tinham sido destruídos, como em Dachau ou Bergen-Belsen.
A velocidade de circulação da informação foi igualmente aproveitada com os avanços tecnológicos da rádio. O cartaz desta exposição, frisa Pacheco Pereira, alude precisamente a esse combate propagandístico, retirado de uma capa de uma revista alemã em que as ondas saídas de dois transmissores confrontam-se. Se a BBC “fazia muita publicidade em português” e começou a implementar “técnicas de propaganda cinzenta”, os alemães “faziam publicidade mais negativa, denunciando as fake news da BBC e a falta de liberdade que havia na imprensa francesa e inglesa”.
Do alinhamento fascista aos ressentimentos britânicos
Em conversa ao Observador, José Pacheco Pereira faz uma admissão curiosa, relacionada com o facto de o espólio da Ephemera já contar com seis quilómetros de estantes divididos por vários armazéns: “A qualidade tem melhor imprensa, mas o que nos permite fazer coisas deste género é a quantidade”. Serve esta declaração para explicar que, ao percorrer toda a coleção destinada a esta mostra, apercebeu-se que “a propaganda produzida não é equilibrada”. “Há muito mais propaganda alemã, quase que não há italiana e há depois um núcleo muito importante de propaganda da Inglaterra e dos Estados Unidos e muito pouca coisa da França”, afirma.
De todos os conjuntos de materiais exibidos em A Outra Guerra, talvez o mais fascinante seja aquele em que a propaganda apresentada é produzida pelos próprios portugueses. É aí, ao ler títulos como “Porque Admiro a Alemanha” (de Holbeche Castelo Branco) ou “Acuso a Inglaterra!” (de Afonso de Albuquerque), que fica bem aparente que a maior parte das simpatias do Estado Novo residia no Eixo.
Dada a natureza firmemente anti-comunista do Estado Novo, não é surpreendente a ausência de materiais de propaganda soviética disseminados neste período, já que eram prontamente intercetados pela censura. No entanto, visto que o regime decalcou a sua tendência conservadora e autoritária mais ao estilo do fascismo de Mussolini do que do nazismo de Hitler, não deixa de ser curioso haver muito mais material propagandístico germânico do que italiano, até porque a Salazar nunca agradou “a coreografia” dos nazis em volta de tendências paganistas.
“Não aparece nada significativo de Itália. Até alguma propaganda italiana que nós temos aqui surge em revistas alemãs, não propriamente em revistas italianas”, revela Pacheco Pereira, adiantando que a questão terá a ver sobretudo com a capacidade superior do regime nazi de produzir propaganda face ao fascismo romano.
Um exemplo dessa sofistificação, aponta, é como os nazis se serviram da história recente entre Portugal e Inglaterra para produzir propaganda anti-britânica especificamente moldada aos ressentimentos portugueses. “Os alemães usam a nossa história, principalmente o Ultimato Inglês, e apresentam a Inglaterra como um país esclavagista, que cometeu massacres nas suas colónias, como no Egipto”, sublinha. Além disso, começam também a produzir textos que “podiam ser lidos hoje sem que as pessoas identificassem a origem”, já que denunciam “o imperialismo britânico” na sua “exploração colonial e económica, nas violências sobre os nativos no racismo”.
Em simultâneo, o regime nazi começou também a desenvolver técnicas inovadoras de propaganda tendo Portugal como alvo, como o financiamento de um selo editorial, a Editora Alma, onde alguns dos autores portugueses acima mencionados, “profundamente anti-ingleses e inteiramente a favor dos alemães”, publicavam as suas diatribes. Ou na forma como “produziram números falsos da revista da Marinha inglesa, a Neptuno, onde a capa era igual, mas abria-se e era só navios ingleses e americanos a ser afundados”. Este tipo de contrafação contrastava com as queixas da natureza injuriosa dos Aliados, como quando, perante uma notícia de que Hering Goering tinha perdido as pernas num ataque, criaram um postal onde se lia um provérbio bem português: “mais depressa se apanha um mentiroso que um coxo”.
Entre doações e alfarrabistas, como se montou o acervo
Visto que o Arquivo Ephemera nasceu do seu próprio espólio pessoal que foi construindo ao longo dos anos, José Pacheco Pereira já tinha alguns materiais portugueses alusivos à Segunda Guerra Mundial antes de se lançar nesta empresa. No entanto, desde então, a coleção “rapidamente cresceu”, fruto de doações e compras em leilões e alfarrabistas.
O mais fácil de encontrar, conta, foram as diversas revistas. A Guerra Ilustrada e o Em Guarda, do lado dos aliados, assim como as alemãs A Esfera e O Sinal “eram muito populares” e, portanto, “muito fáceis de encontrar num espólio que tenha uma representação significativa dos anos 40”. O desafio recaiu, na verdade, nos pequenos materiais avulso, como os postais. Nesse caso, foi particularmente proveitoso receber doações relativas a ambos os lados do conflito.
Do lado dos Aliados, por exemplo, a Ephemera recebeu “o espólio de uma família aqui do Barreiro que tem uma grande coleção de materiais sobre Timor”, sendo que “essa família tinha várias gerações e um dos membros tinha sido o primeiro comandante militar de Timor em 1945, com a saída dos japoneses, e portanto vem muito material do Oriente” e, relativamente à guerra, “material essencialmente pró-inglês”.
Já do lado do Eixo, Pacheco Pereira dá o exemplo de quando, há poucos anos, recebeu o telefonema de um enfermeiro a trabalhar num lar, sinalizando que estava a cuidar de um casal que lhe tinha pedido para entrar em contacto com a Ephemera porque tinha “um grande espólio da guerra, no Norte do país”. “Nós fomos, falámos com os senhores e o espólio era de uma senhora alemã e, portanto, tinha essencialmente material pró-alemão” revela.
Têm sido doações desta natureza o que tem permitido à Ephemera continuar a crescer e a adicionar quilómetros às filas de estantes que o Observador viu na sua visita aos arquivos. No entanto, não obstante o incremento de espaço que esta associação cultural tem vindo a receber por parte da Arco Ribeirinho Sul, que gere o Parque Empresarial do Barreiro, A Outra Guerra vai ocupar um outro local novo, a inaugurar com esta mostra: chama-se Armazém 150 e vai incluir ainda uma outra exposição a abrir ao público também esta terça-feira: O Som é Silêncio, do 18—25 Research Studio, coletivo responsável por parte dos conteúdos apresentados no pavilhão português na Bienal de Arquitetura de Veneza 2025.

title: Você sabe onde o SUS está presente no nosso dia a dia?
content:
De acordo com a Constituição federal de 1988, a “saúde é direito de todos e dever do Estado”. Por isso, da consulta no postinho até uma cirurgia de alta complexidade, o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) está presente na vida de 150 milhões de brasileiros de forma integral. Considerando também os serviços ofertados aos mais de 50 milhões de beneficiários de planos de saúde, que também usam o SUS, soma-se um total de 2,8 bilhões de atendimentos por ano, realizados por 3,5 milhões de profissionais.
Sua rede, de acordo com o Ministério da Saúde, contempla desde ações de promoção e prevenção até atendimentos especializados, procedimentos de alta complexidade e transplantes, atendendo a população em diferentes etapas da vida. Para isso, o SUS segue os princípios da universalização, equidade e integralidade. Mas você sabe onde mais podemos encontrar a atuação do SUS?
Em lugares que você nem imagina
Apesar de só ser acessado na integralidade por 76% dos brasileiros, de uma forma ou de outra, o SUS faz parte da garantia de saúde na vida de todos nós. Podemos nem notar, mas o Sistema atua em ações essenciais para garantir a saúde da população.
É o SUS que faz o controle de qualidade da água potável que chega às nossas casas e do esgoto, por causa das verminoses, através do Programa Nacional de Vigilância da Qualidade da Água para Consumo Humano (Vigiagua). A Vigilância em Saúde Ambiental (VSA) — guarda-chuva que incluí o Vigiagua — é o conjunto de ações que monitora e controla os fatores do meio ambiente que podem afetar a saúde humana. É pela atuação da VSA que é realizado o monitoramento de riscos ligados a possíveis contaminações da água, solo e ar; controlam-se animais e outros vetores de doenças; e são realizadas medidas de resposta a secas, enchentes ou acidentes industriais.
Ainda no âmbito da vigilância, é pelo SUS que se estrutura a Vigilância Sanitária e a Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa). Por elas, o sistema está presente nos mercados, bares, lanchonetes e restaurantes, realizando a fiscalização da qualidade e controle dos alimentos oferecidos pelos estabelecimentos. Quando estes não obedecem às práticas de segurança, é também dever do SUS a intervenção nos estabelecimentos.
A mesma coisa vale para o controle na qualidade dos medicamentos. O SUS normatiza, controla e fiscaliza produtos, substâncias e serviços de interesse para a saúde. Isso significa que, para ser vendido no Brasil, todo medicamento precisa ter autorização da Anvisa.
É igualmente através dessas instituições de fiscalização que o sistema está presente em rodoviárias, portos e aeroportos de todo o Brasil, já que, dada a circulação de pessoas, estes são ambientes de fácil propagação de doenças. Por isso, o sistema é responsável pela fiscalização de normas sanitárias e adoção de medidas preventivas e de controle de surtos, epidemias e agravos à saúde pública naqueles locais.
Nos portos, a Anvisa atua na fiscalização de importações, exportações e circulação de matérias-primas e mercadorias sujeitas à Vigilância Sanitária. No transporte terrestre, cabe à agência a manutenção das boas práticas relativas à oferta de alimentos, gestão de resíduos sólidos e dejetos líquidos.
Caso uma emergência ocorra e você precise acionar o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU), o SUS também estará lá. Criado em 2004 com finalidade de prestar socorro à população em casos de emergência, o serviço tem a gestão feita por estados e municípios, mas a metade do custeio é financiada pelo SUS, através do Ministério da Saúde. Uma curiosidade é que, antes mesmo de ser implantado em todo o Brasil, o Samu foi estruturado de maneira pioneira em Belo Horizonte, em 2003, servindo de referência para o plano nacional.
Através da Subsecretaria de Vigilância, Fiscalização Sanitária e Controle de Zoonoses (Subvisa), o SUS também atua diretamente na vida e manutenção da saúde dos Pets. É por essa estrutura que o Sistema fiscaliza o cumprimento das normas sanitárias nos pet shops. Sendo ainda responsável pela imunização de animais, castração, controle de pragas, prevenção e controle de doenças de animais urbanos e rurais.
O Brasil também tem um amplo sistema de transplante de órgãos, que é referência mundial. É via SUS que são realizadas 96% das cirurgias deste tipo no país, além de garantir a assistência integral ao paciente transplantado. Da mesma forma, os hemocentros, que compõem um dos maiores sistemas públicos de hemoterapia do mundo, são organizados pela Política Nacional de Sangue e Hemoderivados, diretamente vinculada ao SUS.
No mesmo sentido, é consolidada via SUS a maior rede de bancos de leite do mundo. De acordo com o Ministério da Saúde, atualmente existem no país 221 bancos de leite humano e 186 postos de coleta. É assim que toda lactante pode doar leite, desde que esteja saudável e não esteja tomando nenhum medicamento que interfira na amamentação.
O SUS oferece também, gratuitamente, cirurgias e procedimentos ambulatoriais para pacientes que desejam fazer a readequação de gênero. Entre os serviços, estão cirurgia plástica mamária reconstrutiva, cirurgia de redesignação sexual, cirurgia de mastectomia e cirurgia de tireoplastia (troca de timbre de voz). Da mesma forma, são realizadas cirurgias plásticas reparadoras para sequelas e lesões decorrentes de atos de violência contra a mulher.
Invenções brasileiras em saúde
É por meio dessa imensa estrutura de saúde pública que muitas inovações são possibilitadas e implantadas em nosso cotidiano. É o caso dos Agentes Comunitários em Saúde (ACS), profissionais do SUS que fazem o elo direto entre os moradores da comunidade e as Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBS). São eles e elas que realizam as visitas domiciliares, orientam os cidadãos, acompanham grupos vulneráveis e identificam riscos.
Tendo seu projeto piloto em 1987 em alguns estados do nordeste, essa política pública foi nacionalmente implantada a partir de 1991. Quando o Ministério da Saúde (MS), em parceria com as secretarias estaduais e municipais, institucionalizou o Programa Nacional de Agentes Comunitários de Saúde (PNACS). Posteriormente, em 1994, o modelo foi substituído pelo Programa de Saúde da Família (PSF), que, até hoje, oferta uma equipe composta por um médico, um auxiliar de enfermagem, um enfermeiro e seis ACSs.
De acordo com a legislação, o ACS deve ser morador da área em que atua há pelo menos dois anos. Com o tempo, esse profissional tornou-se um importante elemento na promoção da assistência e fortalecimento da atenção básica.
Os ambulatórios de rua, como são popularmente conhecidos os oficiais Consultório na Rua (eCR), são outro exemplo de inovação bem sucedida neste sistema de proporções continentais. O serviço itinerante é voltado para o atendimento integral à população em situação de rua. Segundo o Ministério da Saúde, a política visa ampliar o acesso dessa população, que se encontra em condições de vulnerabilidade e com os vínculos familiares interrompidos ou fragilizados nos serviços de saúde.
Estudos apontam que a iniciativa reduz a dependência de serviços de urgência e emergência, que são mais custosos e menos eficazes para cuidado longitudinal; facilita a detecção precoce de agravos crônicos e demandas psiquiátricas associadas à vulnerabilidade social; promove vínculos e continuidade de cuidado; e reforçam a efetivação dos princípios do SUS.
Embora não exista um consenso global sobre métricas precisas de desempenho, avaliações municipais indicam que o serviço já atendeu milhares de pessoas. O que, em última instância, tende a reduzir internações evitáveis e diminuir pressão sobre serviços de urgência, além de criar oportunidades para cuidado continuado e coordenação com outras políticas públicas.
Novos investimentos em inovação
Na perspectiva do aproveitamento dessas inovações e na integração e efetividade possibilitada por novas tecnologias, tem se inserido no SUS novas práticas que fortalecem a saúde digital. É pensando no melhor atendimento da população, na redução das filas e superlotação que o Departamento de Saúde Digital e Inovação coordena estratégias de telemedicina, telessaúde e o uso de prontuários informatizados para integrar o atendimento básico aos hospitais.
Para que tudo isso seja possível é central a priorização da saúde e o correto investimento no financiamento do sistema. Embora o Brasil apresente um dos menores financiamentos per capita, quando comparado a outros países que buscam ofertar uma saúde pública universal, como França e Reino Unido, recentemente tem sido anunciado novos investimentos em inovação.
É o caso, por exemplo, do anúncio do Ministério da Saúde, este ano, de R$60 milhões voltados à geração de conhecimento científico, tecnologias e soluções inovadoras relacionadas à endometriose, à dor pélvica e à saúde menstrual. Este é o maior investimento já realizado no Brasil pensando na saúde da mulher, em específico.
Neste sentido, especialistas apontam que o fortalecimento do Complexo Econômico-Industrial da Saúde é vital para reduzir a dependência externa e garantir que as necessidades do SUS sejam produzidas no Brasil. Programas como o Novo PAC Saúde expandem a rede com novas UBS, maternidades, policlínicas, unidades móveis e ambulâncias do SAMU. Mas é central o fortalecimento e ampla valorização do SUS, que salva vidas diariamente e se mantém como um dos maiores patrimônios sociais do Brasil.

title: Congo rolls out Canadian-developed vaccine to fight Ebola outbreak
content:
Congolese authorities have begun rolling out a Canadian-developed vaccine in an attempt to protect 20,000 health workers from a fast-spreading Ebola outbreak, but Ottawa could be doing more to develop vaccines that are effective against the current species of the virus, experts say.
The vaccine, known as Ervebo and manufactured by Merck, was developed at the National Microbiology Laboratory in Winnipeg and has been deployed in outbreaks of the most common Ebola species, known as the Zaire virus. Its protective value against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus – the cause of the latest outbreak − is unknown, but health authorities have decided to try it anyway in a large-scale study.
Ervebo was developed and licensed solely for the Zaire virus, but it is the only Ebola vaccine available in large quantities today. There are no proven vaccines for Bundibugyo.
A leading Canadian vaccine researcher suggested in 2014 that the basic platform of what became Ervebo could be developed to target the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, documents show. The work was never done, and the international focus today has shifted to potential vaccines from other developers.
Ottawa temporarily bars entry for foreigners who visited Congo due to Ebola risk
The current Ebola outbreak has infected more than 7,670 people and killed nearly 3,700 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to official data Monday. It is already the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo’s history and is spreading faster than the world’s biggest outbreak, which killed more than 11,300 people in Liberia, Guinea and Sierra Leone from 2014 to 2016.
The outbreak has been fuelled by armed conflicts in eastern Congo that have destabilized the region and forced thousands of people to flee their homes. The lack of a proven vaccine has hampered the response to the crisis.
The vaccination campaign, launched Saturday, will target 20,000 front-line health workers in the epicentre of the outbreak, Congo’s Ituri and North Kivu provinces, over the next nine to 12 months to see whether Ervebo is effective against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus.
“Preliminary data suggest that it may offer some degree of protection against the virus,” said Guyguy Manangama, an epidemiologist and deputy director of Congo Ebola operations with Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF).
“In a race against time … we must use every tool available to us,” he said in a statement. “Even partial protection could help reduce severe illness and death. However, these potential benefits must be demonstrated scientifically.”
Ebola outbreak is outpacing response efforts, WHO chief says
Judie Alimonti, a scientist at the Winnipeg lab who helped develop Ervebo, wrote in a 2014 internal report that she strongly recommended the use of the same vaccine platform to create vaccines for the Bundibugyo and other Ebola viruses. But she noted that there was a lack of money to support the research work in Canada.
“The scientists would have happily continued working on it,” said Matthew Herder, a professor and associate director of the Health Justice Institute at Dalhousie University in Halifax.
“It’s just that they had no more funding from the government, so they couldn’t continue to work,” he told The Globe and Mail in an interview. “Canada could do more now − and they could have done more in the past.”
The 2014 report by Dr. Alimonti was obtained under the Access to Information Act by three researchers, including Prof. Herder.
He said he is concerned that Ottawa’s current emphasis on defence spending could reduce its support for health research, including scientific research on Ebola. The government should recognize that diseases such as Ebola are global security issues that could affect Canada, he said.
U.S. plan for Ebola quarantine in Kenya sparks anger
Adam Houston, a medical policy and advocacy adviser at MSF Canada, said the Ervebo trial is a reminder of Canada’s potential role in future vaccine development.
“It is really surprising that, despite the effectiveness of the original Ebola vaccine developed in the Government of Canada’s own laboratory, the Canadian government has been largely absent from efforts to further develop proven Canadian technology to tackle other viruses causing Ebola disease, including Bundibugyo,” he told The Globe.
The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations is funding studies of four potential vaccines for Bundibugyo. One of them, developed by Moderna, is undergoing its first clinical trial at three sites in Canada.
Karine LeBlanc, a spokesperson for Health Canada, said the national lab in Winnipeg is continuing to conduct laboratory research on Ebola to develop vaccines, treatments and diagnostic tests, including possible Bundibugyo vaccines.
Preliminary data from an animal study at the lab, presented to the World Health Organization in July, demonstrated that Ervebo gave ferrets full protection from Bundibugyo, she noted.

title: Saskatchewan mother calls for safer football helmets after son’s head injury
content:
The family of a Saskatchewan high school football player is calling on schools to use better helmets after he suffered a head injury during a game.
Hunter Gronick, a Grade 12 student at Greenall High School in Balgonie, Sask., experienced a head injury during his Sept. 10 football game. His Balgonie Greenall Griffins were away, facing the Swift Current Comprehensive High School Colts.
“He was doing awesome. He didn’t have any major hits that anybody could tell. Then, he just fell onto the field at one point and that was the last play,” Sabrina Gronick, Hunter’s mother said.
“The coach recalls him saying that he couldn’t see, he couldn’t hear and he collapsed, and then started vomiting.”
Hunter was rushed to hospital for a CT scan when paramedics arrived. He was then taken from the hospital in Swift Current to Regina via air ambulance. In Regina, he underwent an hours-long surgery to remove a major portion of his skull, Sabrina told Global News in an interview.
To protect other high school football players in Saskatchewan, and prevent their families from having to go through the same experience as Hunter’s, his family launched the Hunter’s Headstrong Initiative. It calls on Saskatchewan schools to provide better, safer helmets to football players in order to prevent head injuries.
Get weekly health news
“I understand that it’s not a fix,” Sabrina said, noting that the goal of the initiative is to minimize the chance of head injuries. She is waiting for the high schools athletic association to approve the equipment for use in Saskatchewan.
Patrick Neary, a University of Regina professor with the faculty of kinesiology and health studies, said the effects of brain injuries can be severe. He said options like the guardian cap, soft padding that can be attached to the outside of a helmet, may not always successfully prevent head injuries.
“I hope there’s not a false sense of security when people put the guardian cap on,“ the professor said, explaining that the pads may be ineffective because “something exterior to the brain is not necessarily going to prevent that concussion from happening.”
Hunter is now stable, despite the injury’s effects on his brain and brain stem, his mother said.
“He’s very, very, very slowly achieving milestones,” Sabrina said. “He’s still an extremely long ways away from recovery. He can open his eyes, but at the same time he’s not tracking us. Or when he looks at you, it’s almost like he’s looking past you.”
“Hunter will never be the same kind of guy that he was before,” she continued.
He played football at his high school for two years.
“Hunter is very much a go-getter and very much into camaraderie and that kind of stuff. He loves his team. He loves the game,” his mother said.

title: Contentores com ajuda portuguesa chegaram à Venezuela
content:
Chegaram ao estado de La Guaira, Venezuela, dois dos 10 contentores com quase 240 toneladas de ajuda humanitária recolhida em conjunto por várias organizações não governamentais portuguesas, que será distribuída localmente por associações lusas e venezuelanas.
A chegada foi confirmada à agência Lusa por Jesus Testa, porta-voz da Venexos, uma das associações envolvidas na operação, durante a entrega das paletes às distintas associações locais, ato que decorreu na sede da empresa de logística Almacenadora X7, em Maiquetía, La Guaira.
“Esperamos receber aproximadamente 240 toneladas entre alimentos, medicamentos e artigos de higiene pessoal, para serem entregues e distribuídos, na sua maioria, no estado de La Guaira, que é a zona onde ocorreu o epicentro do sismo na Venezuela e onde temos o maior número de pessoas afetadas”, explicou.
Jesus Testa, que é embaixador de Boa Vontade dos Venezuelanos, explicou ainda que se trata de ajuda humanitária que foi recolhida em Portugal continental e na Madeira, num esforço conjunto de várias organizações, que começou assim que ocorreu o duplo sismo de junho.
A iniciativa, disse, foi possível graças à Venexos, à Associação Amigos da Diáspora e dos Emigrantes Madeirenses (AADEM), à Associação Diáspora no Mundo (ADNM), à Cooperativa Luso-latina Huellatina, à Associação Venezuela Amiga, à Venecom e à Associação Luso-venezuelana — Alusven.
A ajuda já recebida foi entregue a 13 associações locais, entre elas, a Sociedade de Beneficência de Damas Portuguesas, o Lar da Terceira Idade Padre Joaquim Ferreira, o Lar Geriátrico de Maracay, a “Regala Una Sonrisa” (Oferece um sorriso), as Peregrinas de El Junquito, a Venexos, a Consulta Salud (Saúde), e a Ajuda-Caritativa.
A 07 de setembro a Associação Amigos da Diáspora e dos Emigrantes Madeirenses (AADEM) anunciou que previa distribuir a luso-venezuelanos afetados pelo duplo sismo de junho, nas próximas semanas, 240 toneladas de ajuda humanitária angariada em Portugal.
O anúncio foi feito à Lusa pelo presidente da AADEM, Moisés Rodrigues, que esteve em Caracas a tratar do processo de desalfandegamento da ajuda e a verificar a capacidade das associações portuguesas locais para a receber.
Segundo Moisés Rodrigues, “no total, são 10 contentores, sete saídos de Lisboa e três do Porto de Leixões, com uma carga total de 240 toneladas” de ajuda humanitária recolhida pela sociedade civil em Portugal, por venezuelanos e lusodescendentes.
“Nestes contentores temos alimentos, medicamentos, insumos médicos, desde máscaras, luvas, batas, material cirúrgico, fraldas para bebés e adultos, e artigos de uso pessoal”, precisou, sublinhando que a angariação foi feita sabendo que a entrega demoraria algum tempo a chegar à Venezuela, porque o envio seria por via marítima devido a questões de logística internacional.
Entretanto, já foram feitos contactos com associações nas cidades de Los Teques e Valência, além da Cáritas Valência e da Cáritas Caracas, que vão receber a segunda remessa de ajuda humanitária.
“Nesta primeira fase, as organizações já contactadas vão receber entre 10 a 15 paletes cada uma e, por isso, foi importante determinar qual a capacidade instalada de cada uma delas”, frisou Rodrigues.
O duplo sismo de 24 de junho causou danos graves em infraestruturas, feridos e vítimas mortais em sete estados da Venezuela: Caracas, Miranda, Arágua, Carabobo, Lara, Yaracuy e La Guaira, este último o mais afetado.
Segundo o último balanço atualizado divulgado pelas autoridades, 6.509 pessoas morreram e 226.696 feridos foram assistidos nos hospitais venezuelanos depois dos sismos.
Entre as vítimas mortais, há pelo menos 138 portugueses e lusodescendentes.

title: Vor 500 Jahren huldigten die Aarauer mit dem Bachfischet der Lebensader der Stadt, heute führt diese Tradition die Menschen zusammen
content:
Vor 500 Jahren huldigten die Aarauer mit dem Bachfischet der Lebensader der Stadt, heute führt diese Tradition die Menschen zusammen
Ende September ziehen in Aarau immer Tausende Kinder mit selbstgebastelten Lampions durch die dunkle Stadt. Der Brauch gilt als einer der ältesten der Schweiz. Wieso er heute aktueller denn je ist.
Wer in Aarau aufwächst, der ist je nach Jahreszeit prägenden Erlebnissen ausgesetzt: Im Frühling vergeigt der örtliche Fussballklub jeweils den Aufstieg in die Super League, die Sommerferien beginnen mit dem rauschenden Stadtfest, dem Maienzug. Und wenn es wieder früher dämmert und kühler wird, steht der Bachfischet vor der Tür. An diesem Freitag feiert der Brauch sein 500-Jahr-Jubiläum.
Zwar wird im Stadtbach längst nicht mehr geangelt. Trotzdem ist der Bachfischet ein Fixpunkt im Jahr, so sicher wie Ostern, Weihnachten und Silvester: Am vorletzten Freitag vor den Herbstferien gehen um 20 Uhr 15 sämtliche Lichter der Innenstadt aus. Ab dann hellen die Lampions der Kindergarten- und Schulkinder die Gassen auf. Mit den selbstgebastelten Laternen an den Haselruten ziehen sie durch die Altstadt. Je kunstvoller das Sujet der Klasse, desto grösser der Applaus der Tausenden von Menschen auf den Trottoirs. Eine Jury kürt pro Jahrgang ein Siegerprojekt.
Am Ende des Umzugs gibt es Ghackets mit Hörnli, ein grosses Feuer knistert, und das Feuerwerk, der «Mords-Chlapf», besiegelt knapp zwei Stunden später das Ende des Anlasses. Stadtpräsident Hanspeter Hilfiker sagt: «Es ist ein kurzes Fest, überschaubar, aber stimmungsvoll, originell und mit einem historischen Bezug.»
Fälschlich als Unesco-Kulturerbe bezeichnet
Rund um den Bachfischet gibt es Mythen und Legenden. Es heisst etwa, er sei die älteste noch gelebte Tradition in der Schweiz überhaupt. Das ist schwer zu belegen. Die Einsiedler Engelweihe ist seit dem 12. Jahrhundert dokumentiert, der Vogel Gryff und die Fasnacht in Basel ab dem 13. und 14. Jahrhundert. Und der Bündner Chalandamarz geht womöglich sogar auf die römische Besetzung zurück.
Ganz sicher ist diese Aarauer Besonderheit zumindest einer der ältesten Schweizer Bräuche. 2012 wurde der Bachfischet vom Bundesamt für Kultur auf die von der Unesco initiierte «Liste der lebendigen Traditionen in der Schweiz» gesetzt. In den Lokalmedien führte das zu der Falschmeldung, dass der Brauch zum immateriellen Kulturerbe der Unesco zähle.
Das zeigt, wie viel Enthusiasmus und Stolz für diesen urchigen Anlass vorhanden ist. Denn er geht weit in die Annalen der Kleinstadt zurück. Am 3. September 1526 wurde er erstmals im Ratsprotokoll erwähnt. «Item uf hutt hatt man den Bach abgeschlagen», hiess es darin.
Für Mühlen und Feuerwehr
Der Bach, das war die Lebensader der Stadt, die zwar in der Nähe, aber nicht direkt an der Aare liegt. Zum Schutz vor Hochwasser und Feinden hatten die Kyburger ihre neue Siedlung im 13. Jahrhundert auf einer Anhöhe gegründet. Das Wasser leiteten sie vom Fluss Suhre durch einen künstlichen Kanal bis nach Arowe, wie die Stadt in ersten Dokumenten genannt wurde. Der Bach schlängelte sich durch ihre Gassen, lieferte Wasser zum Trinken und Kochen sowie für die Räder der Mühlen. Und er bot den Einwohnern Schutz im Fall von Feuersbrünsten. Dank ihm war das Löschwasser griffbereit.
Diese wichtige Quelle musste sauber gehalten werden. Einmal im Jahr wurde sie eben «abgeschlagen». Die Menschen stoppten den Bach im benachbarten Suhr ausserhalb der Stadt. Davor durften die Kinder ausnahmsweise in ihm fischen. War der Bach einmal trockengelegt, befreiten die Bürger in Fronarbeit vier Tage lang das Bachbett von Dreck und Sand. Ausgefischt und gesäubert, sprudelte das Wasser wieder in Richtung Stadt.
Das war ein Grund zum Feiern. Mit dem Wasser kehrte Leben in die Stadt zurück. Erste Belege für Feste nach der Reinigung des Baches gibt es ab dem 17. Jahrhundert. Wer mitangepackt hatte, bekam im Rathaus einen Trunk. Irgendwann begann der Brauch, seine heutige Gestalt anzunehmen. Die Kinder begleiteten den Bach mit leuchtenden Kürbissen und Räben von Suhr bis nach Aarau. Manche setzten Schiffchen mit Kerzen ins Wasser. «Füürio, de Bach brönnt», singen noch heute lauthals die Klassen während ihres Umzugs.
Zwei Siegerprojekte aus dem Jahr 2025: Die gekleisterten Barbapapas und die Fliegenpilze aus PET-Flaschen erhielten von der Jury je einen Preis.
Aus der Zeit der Helvetik im auslaufenden 18. und beginnenden 19. Jahrhundert finden sich viele Erzählungen darüber, wie vorerst vor allem Buben mit Trommeln und Freudenschreien von Suhr ins Zentrum zogen. Aarau war seinerzeit fünf Monate Hauptstadt der damaligen Helvetischen Republik. Anlässe wie die Jugendfeste – und in Aarau der Maienzug – entwickelten sich gerade in jener Zeit aus ihrem heidnischen Hintergrund zu einem institutionalisierten Anlass. Das galt wohl auch für den Bachfischet.
Der Aargauer Publizist und Historiker Pirmin Meier erklärt den Brauch des Bachfischet auch im Kontext der Reformation. «Mit der Abschaffung vieler Kirchenfeste entstand bei den Reformierten ein Vakuum», sagt Meier. Das sei mit ein Grund, warum in Zürich das Sechseläuten und das Knabenschiessen so wichtig seien.
Ein Kinderbuch erklärt den Brauch
Obwohl heute alle Mädchen und Buben der Stadt mit ihren Ruten durch die dunkle Altstadt ziehen, ist vielen die Geschichte dahinter nicht bewusst. Die Standortförderung der Stadt wollte dies ändern. Sie rief die Idee eines Kinderbuches ins Leben. Katja Schlegel, langjährige Journalistin der «Aargauer Zeitung», setzte in den vergangenen zwei Jahren das Projekt als Autorin um.
Am 3. September, exakt 500 Jahre nach der Erstnennung der Bachreinigung im Ratsprotokoll, ist «Ida und der Bachfischet» mit Text von Schlegel und Zeichnungen der Aarauer Illustratorin Corinne Brunner erschienen. Auf sechzehn Seiten erzählt das Buch, wie Ida aufgeregt und etwas ehrfürchtig dem Bachfischet-Abend entgegenfiebert. Um sie zu beruhigen, nimmt ihr Grosi sie auf den Schoss und erklärt ihr anhand von historischen Figuren den eigentlichen Brauch. Im Anhang finden die Erwachsenen eine Doppelseite mit historischem Hintergrundwissen.
Inzwischen ist Katja Schlegel bei der Standortförderung für die Stadtführungen verantwortlich. Sie sagt: «Häufig bleibt in den Schulen wenig Raum, um die Geschichte unserer Stadt und ihrer Traditionen zu erklären.» Als Journalistin habe sie auf historische Texte immer viele Rückmeldungen erhalten. «Die Menschen wollen heute wissen, woher sie kommen.» Sie habe gemerkt, dass dieses Bewusstsein gepflegt werde. Es sei deshalb umso schöner, dass das Buch etwas klarmache: «Der Bachfischet ist nicht einfach ein Räbeliechtli-Umzug, wir feiern damit die Lebensgrundlage dieser Stadt.»
Vor dem Aussterben gerettet
Irgendwann war dieses Grundbedürfnis selbstverständlich geworden und der Bachfischet obsolet. Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts wäre der Brauch fast ausgestorben. Der Stadtbach hatte seine Bedeutung verloren. Inzwischen gab es längst Leitungen in die Haushalte, die Industrie funktionierte mit Elektrizität. Der Bach verschwand in der Altstadt teilweise unter der Strasse – Platz frei für die ersten motorisierten Fahrzeuge. In der Zwischenkriegszeit fehlte Geld. Anfang der 1920er Jahre war der Bachfischet-Umzug zu einer unbedeutend kleinen Schar geschrumpft.
Das missfiel den Traditionalisten. 1922 entstand aber die Heinerich-Wirri-Zunft, mitbegründet vom umstrittenen rechtskonservativen Chirurgen Eugen Bircher. Die Zunft setzte sich zum Ziel, «etwas Farbe in das philiströse Leben der Kleinstadt» zu bringen und «die Kraft zu gebrauchen zur Erhaltung von alten Sitten und Gebräuchen». Das gelang ihr mit dem Bachfischet. Noch heute übernimmt die Zunft das Patronat über den Brauch und ist die treibende Kraft dahinter, nicht die Stadt.
Andreas Gersbach ist Rechtsanwalt und der Bachfischet-Obmann der Zünfter. Er kennt den Brauch aus der eigenen Kindheit als prägendes Erlebnis. «Ich erinnere mich an die Nervosität, an die mysteriös verdunkelte Stadt, aber besonders auch ans Basteln der Lampions in der Klasse. Wir hatten ein gemeinsames Projekt, das unseren Zusammenhalt förderte.»
Heute ist Gersbach Vorsteher der Jury, die die Laternen prämiert. In den Tagen nach dem Umzug besucht er die Siegerklassen und überreicht ihnen Urkunden. Der Jubel sei jeweils gross und sehr authentisch. Da merke er, welch integrative Kraft im Anlass stecke. «Der Bachfischet verbindet die Leute mit der Stadt, mit der Tradition und untereinander.»
Das 500-Jahr-Jubiläum bietet zusätzlichen Anlass dazu. Eingeladen sind Delegationen anderer alter Bräuche wie etwa der Basler Fasnacht oder des Chalandamarz. Eine weitere Aarauer Institution, der Rüeblimärt, wird sich auch am Umzug zeigen, selbst der FC Aarau ist vertreten. Er hat ein Spezialtrikot zum Bachfischet geschaffen, und einige Profifussballer haben an einer Laterne mitgebastelt. Am Umzug werden sie nicht teilnehmen. Sie spielen zur selben Zeit in Winterthur – vielleicht, um einen besseren Ausgang im Vergleich zu den vergangenen Saisons zu erreichen.

title: Akdital acquires majority stake in Mecca hospital, launches Saudi operations
content: According to a statement obtained by Le360, the facility will now operate under its new brand and corporate identity, Akdital Mecca.“This deal marks a major milestone in the group’s regional expansion in Saudi Arabia and reflects its firm commitment to contributing to the sustainable development of the country’s healthcare system, in line with the ambitious economic and development goals of Saudi Vision 2030,” the statement said.Commenting on the acquisition, Dr. Rochdi Taleb, CEO of Akdital, said the deal represents the successful transition from strategic planning to implementation.Akdital enters Saudi market with first hospital in Riyadh“Completing this acquisition marks a successful transition from strategic planning to implementation on the ground. Akdital Mecca is expected to play a central role in our expansion strategy in the Kingdom,” he said.“Our vision is to turn the facility into a leading medical center that combines clinical excellence, the highest patient safety standards and high-quality services, while fully integrating with the local healthcare system. The scale of the planned investment clearly reflects our long-term vision and our determination to play a key role in strengthening and developing healthcare services in Saudi Arabia,” he added.Comprehensive investment program launched to upgrade and expand hospitalFollowing the acquisition, Akdital has launched a major investment program to overhaul the hospital’s infrastructure and increase its bed capacity.According to the statement, the hospital’s total capacity is expected to rise to 126 beds once the development work is completed, up from 120 currently. The investment program also includes a comprehensive upgrade of its medical and technical infrastructure, a redesign of patient-care pathways to improve operational efficiency, and expanded capabilities in emergency care, intensive care, cardiology, surgery, and maternal and child health.Fez-Meknes brings hospitals, health centers under single regional managementThe planned facilities and capacity include 19 specialized emergency care units, including two clinical resuscitation units; 18 multidisciplinary resuscitation beds; eight cardiac intensive care beds; seven neonatal resuscitation beds, including one isolation bed; 13 nursery beds; seven advanced main operating rooms; one dedicated obstetrics operating room; one endoscopy room; and four delivery rooms.The hospital will also have an integrated medical imaging platform and a specialized medical laboratory.As a multispecialty hospital, Akdital Mecca will provide advanced healthcare services in areas including cardiology, interventional cardiology, general surgery, intensive care and resuscitation, obstetrics and gynecology, neonatology, emergency medicine and medical imaging.Dr. Shadi El Masri, Akdital’s medical director in Saudi Arabia, said the healthcare market in Mecca has unique needs, with the city having to serve both its growing resident population and the increasing number of pilgrims visiting throughout the year.“Saudi Arabia welcomed more than 18 million Umrah pilgrims and international Hajj pilgrims in 2025, and aims to increase its capacity to 30 million visitors a year by 2030,” he said.“In this context, Akdital Mecca will bring real added value to the holy city by offering a broad range of medical specialties, increased capacity in emergency and critical care, as well as rigorous medical governance designed to ensure operational flexibility during peak periods and periods of high patient flows,” he added.Through the strategic acquisition, Akdital plans to draw on its healthcare expertise to serve Mecca residents and pilgrims while contributing to higher quality standards, modernizing medical infrastructure, transferring knowledge and developing local skills.New 33-story university hospital nears completion in Morocco’s capitalAkdital develops and operates a broad network of multispecialty and specialized healthcare facilities. The group currently has a capacity of 4,864 beds across 45 healthcare facilities in 26 cities throughout Morocco.Its workforce currently stands at 10,256 employees across its facilities, including 362 people recruited since the beginning of 2026.Following its successful listing on the Casablanca Stock Exchange in December 2022 under the ticker AKT, Akdital continues to pursue its expansion strategy, with plans to grow its network and strengthen its position in the healthcare sector.

title: Late voting push takes Morocco turnout to 38.02% as parties watch the count
content: A late burst of voting pushed turnout in Morocco’s legislative elections to 38.02pc on Wednesday, bringing down the curtain on an 11-hour polling day and sending parties into the wait for the count.At 5pm, with two hours to go, turnout was still at 28.05pc. Nearly 10 percentage points were added before polling stations shut at 7pm.It had been a much slower affair in the morning. Only 4.23pc of registered voters had turned up by 10am. The figure reached 11.34pc at noon before the afternoon brought more voters through the doors.The final 38.02pc figure was compiled from returns received from prefectures, provinces and district prefectures across the country, the Interior Ministry said.Voting went ahead normally across Morocco apart from a few isolated incidents at a limited number of polling stations, according to the ministry.By Wednesday evening, the queues had given way to the count.Ballot boxes were opened as soon as polling ended, with representatives of candidate lists present as votes began to be sorted and tallied. Local constituency votes are counted first, followed by those for the regional constituencies.The paperwork then moves up the chain. Polling stations send their official minutes to central polling offices, which consolidate the votes cast for each list.Counting committees headed by judges will use those returns to determine the results and declare the winners.At stake are all 395 seats in the House of Representatives and, beyond them, the balance of power after a campaign in which even the three parties that governed together for the past five years—RNI, PAM and Istiqlal—fought hard for their own share of the electorate. The campaign ended at midnight on Tuesday. By 7pm Wednesday, the voters had had their say. Now comes the arithmetic .

title: How New Zealand’s Asian communities celebrate a mid-autumn festival in spring
content:
Asian communities nationwide are marking mid-autumn celebrations in their own ways.
The celebrations fall on the 15th day of the eighth month of the lunar calendar, a time traditionally associated with harvests and a full moon in the Northern Hemisphere.
In Auckland, a three-day Moon Festival is poised to begin on Friday.
The event marks the arrival of the Mid-Autumn Festival, known as Zhongqiu Jie (中秋节) in Chinese, one of the most important celebrations in the Chinese calendar.
However, the festival is only one expression of much broader traditions.
South Korean, Japanese and Vietnamese communities across the country are also observing the season through customs shaped by their own history, food and family rituals.
In Vietnam, the celebration is called Tết Trung Thu and is often described as a festival for children.
This year, Tết Trung Thu falls on Friday.
In Lower Hutt, the Vietnamese community plans to mark the occasion a day later with the Moonlit Memories Festival at Te Mako Naenae Community Centre.
Vinh Nguyen, director of event organiser Viet Hub NZ, said the festival would give the wider community a chance to experience the atmosphere of celebrations he remembered from childhood.
Activities are set to include lion dancing, bánh Trung Thu (mooncakes), star lanterns, Vietnamese crafts and masks, children's games, storytelling, food and cultural performances.
Nguyen said the festival had long held a special place in Vietnamese culture.
She said the celebration allowed Vietnamese children growing up in New Zealand to maintain a connection to tradition.
"I think that says a lot about the migrant experience. Home may look different now, but our stories, traditions and memories travel with us," she said.
"And I hope our children grow up knowing that they don't have to choose between being Kiwi and being Vietnamese. They can be both and be proud of both."
New Zealand's South Korean community celebrates Chuseok, also known as Hangawi, at the same time of year.
It's one of South Korea's most important traditional holidays.
Falling on Friday this year, Chuseok will be marked at several schools and universities across New Zealand, giving Korean students and families a chance to celebrate the holiday away from home.
Long Bay College in Auckland will mark the occasion on Friday with traditional Korean food and games, while the University of Canterbury Korean Society is planning a Chuseok Festival on Saturday that will include cultural performances and activities.
Soo Jung, vice-president of the University of Canterbury Korean Society, said the festival had been held annually on campus since 2023.
This year's programme will feature samul nori (a modern form of traditional Korean percussion performed with four instruments), buchaechum (a traditional Korean fan dance), a gumdo sword arts demonstration and K-pop dance performances.
Visitors will also have the chance to sample traditional festival food, including songpyeon - half-moon-shaped rice cakes with a variety of fillings, traditionally steamed over pine needles and said to symbolise growth and progress.
Jung said the event would give people from across Christchurch an opportunity to experience South Korean culture and traditions together.
"It is definitely a great opportunity for Kiwis, and people from any background, to experience Korean culture in a fun and welcoming environment," Jung said.
New Zealand's Japanese community traditionally observes Tsukimi at this time of year.
Literally meaning "moon viewing", Tsukimi is a centuries-old tradition of gathering to admire the large celestial body in the autumn night sky.
Tsukimi falls on Friday, with celebrations including such things as poetry, traditional music and dance.
Food also plays an important role.
Among the best-known offerings is tsukimi dango - small round rice dumplings whose shape evokes the full moon.
In Auckland, libraries and community groups are hosting a series of Tsukimi-themed events this year, bringing Japanese moon-viewing traditions to local families.
At Point Chevalier Library, a Tsukimi celebration will be held on 1 October.
The Japan Kauri Education Trust will also host a Japanese Moon Festival at Ōwairaka Connecting Communities Hub on 28 September, inviting visitors to create their own rabbit-inspired kaleidoscopes and learn about the stories and traditions behind Tsukimi.
This year, some community events are also bringing different cultural traditions together in a single celebration.
At Epsom Community Centre, a Moon Festival on 3 October will combine Chinese and Korean traditions.
Visitors will be able to make Chinese mooncakes and paper lanterns, prepare South Korean songpyeon rice cakes, try on traditional hanbok and take part in a hanbok runway.
Sanjay Pereira, manager of the community centre, said Epsom was home to a large and diverse Asian population, and that festivals tied to the lunar calendar held particular significance for many families in the area.
He said he hoped the event would give Asian families a chance to reconnect with their cultures and customs, while also giving the wider community an opportunity to experience diversity.
Yoona Song, a senior library and council services assistant who helped organise a Moon Festival cultural event at Botany Library on Sunday, said the celebration also brought together people from a wide range of cultural and ethnic backgrounds through traditional games and craft activities from several Asian cultures.
"Our goal was not only to celebrate the Moon Festival," Song said. "We hoped this would encourage greater cultural understanding, curiosity and appreciation within our diverse community."
Although Asian communities mark the season in different ways, Song said events such as the Moon Festival could make those traditions more accessible to people from all backgrounds.
"We hope the event encourages Aucklanders to explore and appreciate the diverse cultures that make up our community, while also fostering a sense of belonging and inclusion," Song said.

title: Every American city needs a music office
content: Cities are spending aggressively to compete for economic growth and cultural relevance. They build entertainment districts, recruit employers, subsidize major developments, and launch branding campaigns designed to attract people to them. While governments turn their eyes to more traditional economic sectors, like technology or manufacturing, they are overlooking a key place-based industry that can’t be outsourced: music. Municipalities are realizing that music is more than entertainment and culture. It’s entrepreneurship and small-business growth. It’s also tourism and commercial real estate, along with global brand building. The cities that treat music as economic infrastructure are seeing measurable returns. That is why municipal music offices need to be seen as quality-of-life and economic development tools designed to organize and strengthen an industry that already exists in nearly every community. MUSIC IS A STRATEGY A music economy already exists in nearly every city. It includes performers and venues, but also educators, engineers, promoters, production companies, record stores, festivals, hospitality businesses, media organizations, nonprofits, and community supporters. The challenge is a fragmented music economy. Tourism agencies market events. Planning departments regulate venues. School systems develop talent. Economic development teams recruit businesses. Arts councils fund programs. Each is doing valuable work, but without coordination, cities miss opportunities. Plus, duplicate efforts unintentionally create barriers to growth. A music office connects those pieces, giving the sector a central point of strategy, accountability, and support. The economic case for doing so is increasingly difficult to ignore. The Texas Music Office set the stage for what government-supported music programs can deliver. The state’s music industry, education sector, and music-related tourism supported nearly 196,000 jobs. It generated $31.7 billion in annual economic activity, while producing approximately $564 million in state tax revenue. The Tulsa Office of Film, Music, Arts, and Culture has bolstered its thriving, organic music scene with structured programs that have enabled local artists to tour, and empowered sustainable music careers with educational programs and networking with the Recording Academy. In Huntsville, an updated analysis by Sound Diplomacy estimates that the direct music sector supports 2,424 jobs, a 145% increase compared with 986 in 2018. The broader music ecosystem now supports 3,047 jobs and generates $278.2 million in total economic output. The city invested $55 million into the Orion Amphitheater, yielding an estimated $85.2 million economic impact during its first 18 months of operation. Those results did not come from simply booking more concerts. They reflect what happens when infrastructure, policy, partnerships, community programming, tourism, entrepreneurship, and long-term workforce development are treated as parts of the same strategy. Music is often seen as only entertainment, but the data is clear: Local investments create jobs. They also drive foot traffic to small businesses and retain young talent. WHAT A MUSIC OFFICE DOES A music office serves as a connector. Its role is to bring the people, organizations, and public resources already shaping it together. By aligning stakeholders from across the ecosystem—from artists to venue operators—a music office helps the sector grow more intentionally, efficiently, and sustainably. The focus—whether live music venues or career development—starts with a coordinated effort and alignment with broader city priorities. Working with tourism boards will amplify music events; collaborating with school systems and universities creates career pipelines; understanding public transit and city ordinances allows for smarter venue planning. Beyond initial integration with other regional priorities, music offices are the ultimate brand ambassadors for cities. Creating artist and influencer ambassador programs creates evangelists for local artists and fans to spread the good word about your city’s music scene, drawing industry investment and tourists alike. And perhaps most importantly, music offices support emerging local artists through a suite of programs. That includes touring grants and connections with studios, as well as career support. THE ROI OF LOCAL SOUND Music offices enable cities to tap into economic activity that lasts for years. While many states and cities have entertainment offices providing tax incentives for shooting or producing films, these incentive types are temporary. Film shoots often last months, at most; in many cases, talent and crews are brought in from other states. Tax incentives for developing music ecosystems, on the other hand, can be built affordably and last for generations. Steady careers in music, as an artist, sound engineer, or in management, create roots in communities that film alone cannot do. The recently formed Association of Music Offices, is filled with examples of cities creatively investing in music infrastructure with real economic results, with support from the Recording Academy. HOW TO APPROACH A MUSIC PROGRAM The most successful municipal-driven music programs begin with the people. Programs should be community-informed and transparent. Holding regular community meetings and outreach to diverse stakeholders is vital to be inclusive and equitable, and also to be authentic. Every city has its own unique sound, and music offices need to listen to their communities to let those sounds ring true. Second, it is important to prioritize local ownership, legacy venue protections, and underrepresented artists in program design. Who has typically been left on the sidelines and needs a megaphone? Where do you have the most impact opportunity? Lastly, do not underestimate the importance of the less exciting aspects of a successful music sector: zoning reform, noise ordinances, and affordability policies needed to accompany cultural investment to prevent gentrification and inequities. MUSIC IS THE NEW CIVIC STANDARD Infrastructure is roads and buildings, but it’s also the ecosystems that help people create, perform, gather, and belong. In 2026, a music office is an essential part of civic infrastructure for cities serious about competitive growth and creative retention. Matt Mandrella is music officer for the City of Huntsville.

title: Ekurhuleni murders: Lesufi welcomes breakthrough in Dawn Park murder investigation
content:
Police have made a breakthrough in the Dawn Park murder case, arresting three suspects over the weekend.
The Gauteng provincial government has hailed the arrest of three suspects in connection with the murder of Jabulile Ntimba, describing the breakthrough as a decisive step in the fight against violent crime.
The arrests follow intensive investigative work by the South African Police Service (Saps).
Police earlier announced a breakthrough had been made in the Dawn Park murder case, arresting three suspects over the weekend, a move the Gauteng government said underscored the power of sustained investigations and community cooperation.
Progress
Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi said the development reflects the importance of persistence and collaboration.
“We welcome the progress made by the investigating team and commend all officers involved. This demonstrates the importance of sustained police investigations, cooperation from communities and decisive action against violent crime.
“We extend our condolences to the family and loved ones of Jabulile Ntimba and reaffirm our commitment to ensuring that victims of violent crime receive justice,” Lesufi said.
Operation Shanela
The provincial government also highlighted ongoing law‑enforcement drives such as Operation Shanela and lockdown operations in Kempton Park and across Ekurhuleni, aimed at disrupting criminal activity, apprehending suspects and restoring community safety.
Provincial government spokesperson Elijah Mhlanga said these operations include targeted interventions such as roadblocks, stop-and-searches, compliance inspections, and intelligence-driven patrols.
“The provincial government will continue to support the implementation and impact of these operations and strengthen coordination between the Saps, Gauteng traffic police, municipalities and other law-enforcement agencies.”
Community engagement
Lesufi urged communities to remain active partners in the fight against crime.
“We welcome this latest breakthrough and urge communities to continue working with law enforcement by providing information that can assist investigations and bring perpetrators of crime to justice.”
Ekurhuleni victims named
Meanwhile, the South African Police Service (Saps) has named the nine victims who were brutally murdered in Ekurhuleni on Gauteng’s East Rand.
Saps disclosed the names on Monday, 21 September, following a major breakthrough in the chilling series of women’s murders.

title: Finding a way to trust the water
content:
Three years after the fall of Saigon in 1975, I came to Australia on a prawn trawler with four other members of my family. Yes, we were among those immigrant boat people. I was a child, led by the hand by parents desperate to leave the only home they’d ever known. Five metres by 18 metres was the size of the vessel; the adults were so crammed in that they were unable to lie down flat for the entire week we were at sea. Seated with knees to chest was the optimum way to fit in as many people as possible. Twice we were chased by pirates. When a storm destroyed the boat, we were rescued by an oil rig ship and taken for asylum processing in Indonesia. Months later, Australia finally accepted us as refugees. I was six.
It was the start of my fear of large bodies of water.
Even though I have very little recollection of the journey here, I have vague muscle memories of unease and fear. Of a tiny boat carried, rocked by forces beyond its control. Of cresting waters and seasickness. Of being at the mercy of the elements. Of clinging to my mother for balance. For life.
If you put any credence in astrology, it’s sufficient to say I am not a Pisces but a Sagittarian. I am fiercely terrestrial; I like my feet grounded as I flex my bow and aim towards the horizon.
Like every child in primary school, I had a couple of swimming lessons. The smell of chlorine was foreign to me and repellent; moving about in a disinfectant held no joy. My tiny goggles were always incorrectly and loosely fastened, so my eyes were stung and reddened. I remember all around me the squeals of my peers as they followed the instructor’s direction to blow bubbles and slice through the shallows like a torpedo. There was always more splashing than there needed to be.
I was one of the trembling ethnic kids at the edge of the pool, tearful when requested to relinquish the bright yellow kickboard I clung to as a buoy. There was no way I was going to let go and drop like a stone into this immeasurable expanse of liquid blue.
I was big-eyed but undersized for my age, shy, quiet and undemanding. With the teacher forever distracted by the ruckus of the other children, I feared if I let go of that kickboard I’d fall, soundless, without anyone realising my mouth had drunk too much, my limbs in uncoordinated disarray, my lungs unable to cope with the deficit of air. The pressure was too great. How ridiculous it would be if I were to drown now in this artificial, temperature-controlled space, after my family had made it safely across perilous seas a few years earlier.
Little by little, over two months of practice, I became slightly less scared of the water and even managed a rudimentary freestyle, backstroke and the oddly titled but serene “chicken, aeroplane and soldier” swimming drills.
At the end of those few lessons, I still hadn’t learnt to swim. I could barely even put my face in the water without having a minor panic attack. Some invisible force would pull me down, I thought, if I didn’t have one hand still hanging onto the plastic railing separating the baby learners from those who’d already mastered this skill of pushing through the blue. Barely a few metres away, the adults did their best to ignore the ragtag squeals of primary-schoolers and focused on their laps in the medium and fast lanes with the efficiency of machines.
The teacher, exasperated by my failure to trust, ended up offering me a snake inflatable and allowing me to hang on to it listlessly while she concentrated on the kids who had more enthusiasm for kicking their legs and stretching their arms in synchronised movements. I watched them from the sidelines with an equal mix of envy and fear, bobbing up and down like a rubber duckie on the momentum of their actions.
I spent the next few decades refusing to put my face in any body of water larger than a shower-bath. I was always on the edge. On a deckchair near the pool, or with my toes immersed in the gentle spray rolling onto the sand. Never fully in or under.
Until this year.
In the impetuous heat of summer, I decided to finally confront this aquaphobia. The local council was offering free swimming lessons to adult women in a targeted multicultural program. I signed up quickly, before anxiety could sway my decision. The instructor was young and cheerful, with broad shoulders. We, her five wards, were short and small and brown, and had names she struggled to pronounce. Most of us were at least 20 years older than her.
Over a few weeks, she took us along a rapid course of breathing exercises and stroke correction, and supported us as we kicked, flailed and spluttered in the heated one-metre-deep kiddie pool. I swallowed way too much chlorine.
Little by little, over two months of practice, I became slightly less scared of the water and even managed a rudimentary freestyle, backstroke and the oddly titled but serene “chicken, aeroplane and soldier” swimming drills.
It was reassuring to see the other newbie swimmers as hesitant as I was in the shallows. There was no sense of competition among us; silently, we cheered each other on as, one by one, in relay form, and under the encouraging eye of the instructor, we did our best to navigate to the end of the pool and back again. In one class, she coaxed us to the much bigger, much colder waters of the adult section and tried to teach us to tread water. This was a new fear to confront, as our feet could no longer touch the bottom of the pool. To keep afloat in the deep, “whisk your legs like an eggbeater”, she told us, “and make figure eights with your hands”.
Hugging my torso with goosepimply arms, I was glad to return to the much warmer kiddie section and to stand again on solid ground.
There was a lot to remember – so many instructions to follow in this complicated business of moving your body and limbs, of controlling the intake of air, and of resisting panic should all these steps fail to coalesce. But the most significant development from these lessons was that – for the first time in my life – I learnt how to float, how to trust, and be held by a body of water, to be rendered weightless.
Outside our formal lessons, I went to the pool alone and would just starfish, looking up at the ceiling. My ears were half submerged so as to muffle the sound of any nearby kids, and my eyes were closed to better concentrate on the sound of my own breath, soft and steady. Sometimes I’d raise one arm up, just for the joy of waving but not drowning. I was buoyant.

title: Right dose, right patient: Clinician-led implementation of a national cross-specialty strategy for immunoglobulin stewardship.
content: Global demand for immunoglobulin (Ig) continues to rise, driven by expanding clinical indications and limited plasma supply. In England, use increased annually despite earlier demand-management efforts, with substantial regional variation and prescribing for indications lacking evidence of benefit. This study reports the outcomes of a national, clinician-led Ig stewardship strategy implemented between 2018 and 2025. National Health Service England introduced a three-part programme comprising a national evidence-based commissioning policy, establishment of 21 Sub-Regional Immunoglobulin Assessment Panels, and enhancement of the National Immunoglobulin Database. The strategy embedded cross-specialty clinical review, standardised approval processes, strengthened dosing guidance and improved national data capture. Outcomes were assessed through national audits, retrospective studies and analysis of usage trends. All panels were operational by 2021, reporting improved governance, multidisciplinary collaboration and coordinated responses to supply pressures. Panel-led reviews enabled safe treatment withdrawal or dose reduction in selected long-term patients. Non-evidence-based prescribing declined from 8.5% to 1.7%. National Ig use fell by 12% over the first 5 years and, despite a recent increase in demand, Ig use in England in 2025 was almost half of the projected use had the stewardship strategy not been implemented. A nationally coordinated, clinician-led stewardship model based on rigorous evidence-based peer review can reduce inappropriate Ig use, optimise dosing, and improve equity of access while delivering substantial cost savings.

title: "Zaboravljene" spolno prenosive bolesti u porastu u Splitu
content:
U posljednjih nekoliko godina u splitskom KBC-u bilježi se porast nekada gotovo zaboravljenih spolno prenosivih bolesti, poput sifilisa i gonoreje. Da se radi o povećanoj incidenciji potvrdila je predstojnica Klinike za kožne i spolne bolesti KBC-a Split doc. dr. sc. Dubravka Vuković.
Oglas
Jedan od mogućih razloga vidi u promjenama spolnog ponašanja, među ostalim i nakon uvođenja profilaktičkih terapija za prevenciju HIV-a.
"Jedan od mogućih utjecaja na povećanu incidenciju posljednjih godina ponovno je slobodnije spolno ponašanje, zahvaljujući i takozvanim profilaktičkim terapijama" kazala je Vuković novinarki Dalmatinskog portala Živani Šušak Živković.
Riječ je o PrEP-u i PEP-u, odnosno terapijama koje se koriste u prevenciji infekcije HIV-om kod određenih rizičnih skupina.
"Kada je HIV na neki način postao kronična bolest, kada su kolege infektolozi to stabilizirali, ljudi su se ponovno opustili i sada ponovno vidimo porast nekih praktički zaboravljenih spolno prenosivih bolesti", rekla je.
Pitali su doktoricu koliko na broj tih spolno prenosivih infekcija u Splitu utječe i činjenica da je riječ o izrazito turističkom gradu.
"Nedavno sam bila na jednom skupu s kolegama iz Osijeka i oni kažu da u svojim ambulantama gotovo uopće ne viđaju spolno prenosive bolesti. Mi smo, kao turistički grad, sigurno tu perjanica, možda u negativnom smislu kada govorimo o tim infekcijama", odgovorila je.
Poseban problem predstavlja i sve veća otpornost uzročnika sifilisa na antibiotike. Konkretno, liječi se penicilinom. Postoji, stoga, mogućnost, upozorila je dr. Vuković, da se u jednom trenutku ostane bez terapijskih opcija.

title: Φρίκη στην Ηλεία: Νεογέννητα κουτάβια βρέθηκαν ζωντανά σε σακούλα μέσα σε κάδο ανακύκλωσης (video)
content:
Ένα νέο, αποτρόπαιο περιστατικό κακοποίησης ζώων έρχεται να προκαλέσει οργή στην κοινή γνώμη. Στον Βρανά Ηλείας, ένας ασυνείδητος δράστης άρπαξε έξι νεογέννητα κουτάβια από την αδέσποτη μητέρα τους, τα έκλεισε ερμητικά μέσα σε μια πλαστική σακούλα και τα πέταξε σαν να ήταν σκουπίδια μέσα σε κάδο ανακύκλωσης, καταδικάζοντάς τα σε έναν αργό και βασανιστικό θάνατο.
Η έγκαιρη και σωτήρια επέμβαση μιας εθελόντριας απέτρεψε την τραγωδία την τελευταία στιγμή, ενώ οι εικόνες που καταγράφηκαν κατά τη διάρκεια της διάσωσης αποτυπώνουν το μεγαλείο της μητρικής αγάπης στον κόσμο των ζώων.
View this post on Instagram
Η έρευνα στον κάδο και ο εντοπισμός της κλειστής σακούλας
Η αντίστροφη μέτρηση για τη σωτηρία των μικρών ξεκίνησε όταν η Γιάννα, μια δραστήρια εθελόντρια από το Βαρθολομιό, ενημερώθηκε για τον εντοπισμό των εγκαταλελειμμένων κουταβιών.
Χωρίς να χάσει χρόνο, έσπευσε στο σημείο και άρχισε να ψάχνει σχολαστικά μέσα στον κάδο ανακύκλωσης. Εκεί, βρέθηκε μπροστά στο θλιβερό θέαμα: μια δεμένη σακούλα, μέσα στην οποία βρίσκονταν τα έξι ανυπεράσπιστα κουτάβια, τα οποία έκλαιγαν απεγνωσμένα για βοήθεια.
Η εθελόντρια τα έβγαλε αμέσως έξω, ενώ παράλληλα ειδοποίησε την Αστυνομία για να καταγραφεί το σοβαρό αυτό αδίκημα, το οποίο πλέον διώκεται σε βαθμό κακουργήματος.
Η συγκλονιστική επανένωση
Κατά τη διάρκεια της διάσωσης, οι παρευρισκόμενοι έγιναν μάρτυρες μιας εξαιρετικά συγκινητικής σκηνής που αποτυπώθηκε και σε βίντεο.
Η αδέσποτη μητέρα των κουταβιών, η οποία περιφερόταν σε κατάσταση απόγνωσης γύρω από τον κάδο ψάχνοντας τα μωρά της, πλησίασε αμέσως μόλις άκουσε τα κλάματά τους. Με απίστευτη τρυφερότητα και προσοχή, η σκυλίτσα πλησίασε, άρπαξε απαλά με το στόμα της ένα από τα μικρά της για να το προστατεύσει και προσπάθησε να το απομακρύνει από το σημείο, αρνούμενη να αποχωριστεί ξανά την οικογένειά της.
Μια αγκαλιά ασφάλειας και έκκληση για βοήθεια
Η περιπέτεια της τετράποδης οικογένειας είχε αίσιο τέλος, καθώς μεταφέρθηκαν σε ασφαλές περιβάλλον. Αυτή τη στιγμή φιλοξενούνται προσωρινά από εθελόντρια της περιοχής, η οποία, παρά τις προσωπικές και οικονομικές της δυσκολίες, φροντίζει δεκάδες αδέσποτα ζώα.
Η ανάγκη για στήριξη είναι πλέον επιτακτική, καθώς τα νεογέννητα και η μητέρα τους χρειάζονται ειδική διατροφή, εμβόλια, ιατρική παρακολούθηση και, πάνω από όλα, ανθρώπους που θα θελήσουν να τους προσφέρουν ένα μόνιμο και ζεστό σπιτικό.
